To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pH of a test solution is measured by an electrode in contact with the test solution and that the measured value is the difference between the pH of the test solution and the pH of the reference electrode.

(i) the method developed for testing glass pH responsive electrodes at 25 ° C in the absence of Na+, K+, Li+ can be extended to 37, 85 and 65 0 C; (ii) the method is suitable for determining alkaline errors at 25 ° and 85 65 0C for Na+, K+, Li+ at up to 0.5, 1, 1 mol dm−3, respectively; (iii

the method is suitable for testing the pH response of electrodes at 25 ° C, 65 ° C and 85 ° C, for the pH range 2 — 11, with an accuracy of about ± 0.01 pH, and for the determination of Na+ and K+ errors at up 1 mol dm 3 cation at 25 °c.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and testing of glass electrodes for use at temperatures up to 100 °C and in the presence of high concentrations of alkali metal cations.
the design and development of new glass electrode systems for use in clinical chemistry and in industrial process control and monitoring.
the development of methods for testing glass electrodes and the determination of their errors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method is applicable to the determination of the pH of solutions of 1 mol dm—3 Na+, K+ or Li+ at 25,37,65 and 85 °C with an accuracy of about ±. 0.03 pH unit, and that the method is capable of determining errors of glass electrodes in the presence of 1 mol.dm—3 cation with an accuracy of at least 0.02 unit.
the pH of a solution can be measured with an error of ± 0.02 at 25 ° C and ± 0.03 at 37 °C.
, at present, there is no satisfactory glass electrode available for use with high concentrations of Na, K+ or Li+ in solutions with pH > 6.5 at temperatures up to 85 0c.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pH errors for the electrodes we tested were within ± 1.0 mV (± 0.02pH) at 25 ° C, ± 2.0 mV at 37 °C, ± 2 mV at 65 °C and ± 3 mV at 85 °C.

it is now possible with a few simple precautions to test glass electrodes with a high degree of reliability and to determine the errors due to alkali metal ions over the whole pH range of clinical interest.

the accuracy and precision of glass electrodes can be improved by about 100 times over the normal range of pH 4-10, and the errors due to Na, K+, and Li+ can be measured with accuracy ± 1 mV (±0.02 pH).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pH response at high pH of glass electrodes with a high sodium content is not affected by the presence of Na+ ions at concentrations of up to 1.5 mol dm3.

the glass electrode is not an ideal device for measuring hydrogen ion concentration at high pH, but that it can be used with confidence in the presence of alkali metal cations up to 1 M Na+ or K+ or 0.5 M Li+.
glass pH electrodes should not be used at temperatures above 37 °C and that the use of electrodes for measuring pH above pH 9.0 should be avoided.
